subject: w349-C005

subject: w349 WEIGHTED_GAP.md posterior factorization counterexample
exact_scope: X=Exp(1)-1, s>0, Y=sX+sqrt(s)Z, independent standard Gaussian Z, fixed f(x)=x. Mathematical strictness only; the reported quadrature value is not independently certified by w350.
independent_reproduction: The posterior is N((y-1)/s,1/s) truncated at -1. At y=1-s its variance is (1-2/pi)/s; as y tends to positive infinity it tends to 1/s. The variance A(y) is continuous, so it is nonconstant. Y has positive density everywhere and 0<A<=1/s, hence Var(A(Y))>0. The proposed bound reduces to E A^2 <= (E A)^2 and is strictly false.
remaining_gap: Does not refute the correctly weighted bound or KLS.

subject: w349 WEIGHTED_GAP.md conditional Gronwall reduction
exact_scope: Full-dimensional compactly supported isotropic log-concave prior; smooth f; assumed uniform T>0 and K>=0 with E|Cov_mu_t(f,X)|^2 <= K E Var_mu_t(f) for almost every t<T.
independent_reproduction: Innovation Y_t-integral a_r dr has zero conditional drift and bracket tI; compact support gives integrability, so Levy identifies a Brownian motion. Bayes/Ito gives d(mu_t f)=Cov_mu_t(f,X).dW_t. Ito isometry and total variance give V(t)=V(0)-integral E|Cov|^2. The assumed inequality implies V(T)>=exp(-KT)V(0). Posterior curvature T gives V(T)<=energy/T by generalized strong-log-concavity Poincare. For extension, truncate an arbitrary prior on expanding balls and whiten. Its means converge to 0 and covariance matrices Sigma_j converge to I; transfer the bound to the unwhitened conditional laws with factor ||Sigma_j||, then pass compact smooth tests to the limit.
remaining_gap: The weighted all-function input and the generalized strong-log-concavity Poincare inequality are explicit external inputs; no parent proof is claimed.

subject: w349-C010 finite-fourth-moment tilt-domain counterexample
exact_scope: R density 5 r^-6 for r>=1, independent fair sign S, X=sqrt(3/5) S R. It is a counterexample to the general moment-only domain assertion, not a log-concave example.
independent_reproduction: Integral_1^infinity 5r^(k-6)dr=5/(5-k) for k<5. Symmetry gives mean 0; scaling gives variance (3/5)*(5/3)=1 and fourth moment (9/25)*5=9/5. For any z!=0, the half with matching sign has an exponential integral against r^-6 and diverges.
remaining_gap: The covariance-operator norm identity remains valid; the parent log-concave route has exponential moments.
